nora: FYI saw repeated read bursts during bundle hydration in canary. Safetensors index-first path tends to enqueue lots of small warmup reads that flush once the token-bucket refills, producing IO spikes and eviction churn. We need a short mitigation plan. :alarm_clock:

diego: Any logs or a tiny repro? Is it correlated with per-tenant rate limits or global disk throughput?

nora: Snippet from one affected pod (abridged):

```\n2026-03-19T11:02:10Z warmup: enqueue shard/3 (1.2GB)
2026-03-19T11:02:10Z rl: tbucket empty, warmup queued (n=18)
2026-03-19T11:02:14Z rl: refill -> dequeue 18
2026-03-19T11:02:14Z io: read_bytes/sec 1.1GB/s
2026-03-19T11:02:15Z evict: 120 pages
2026-03-19T11:02:16Z latency: spike3x
```

This pattern repeats across multiple nodes. Legacy mmapped .bin had smaller bursts but less overall stress.

sam: Two levels of fixes. Short-term: runtime pacing (leaky + jitter) and per-shard priority ordering to fetch critical tensors first. Mid-term: server-side background "hydration ramp" that incrementally pulls bundles during low IO windows.

diego: We must be careful with manifestless streaming bundles where chunk contiguity matters. Any pacing needs to avoid excessive seeks. For safetensors (index-first) we can prioritize by layer offsets. For streaming, pace contiguous chunks together.

tara: Also, encryption. A couple tenants use KMS and decryption costs are CPU-limited. Bursts create CPU contention. We should surface a `decrypt_cost_ms_per_mb` metric and optionally a `decrypt_rate` hint in the manifest.

ops-bot: Incident created: CANARY-2026-03-19-hydration-thrash. Linked to thread.

nora: Proposal idea for manifest hints (keeps surface tiny):
```
"hydration_policy": "ramp|burst|off",
"hydration_rate_mb_s": "30",
"hydration_priority": "kv_first|layered|flat",
"decrypt_rate_mb_s": "optional"
```
Default behavior is unchanged unless hints present.

sam: Runtime agent prototype pseudocode for leaky ramp: 
```
rate = manifest.hydration_rate_mb_s or global_default
while q.not_empty():
  req = q.pop_front()
  if not rate_limiter.allow(req.size):
    wait_ms = compute_wait(req.size, rate)
    sleep(wait_ms + small_jitter())
    q.push_front(req)
    continue
  start_prefetch(req)
  // optional small spacing to avoid bus saturation
  sleep(space_ms)
```
We should compute `space_ms` dynamically from recent io_samples to react to real throughput.

diego: For shadow/background hydration: spawn a low-priority worker per-pod that runs when cpu_io_headroom > threshold and `hydration_policy==ramp`. It should not compete with live request reads (IOScheduler nice-level). Keep it disabled by default.

tara: Telemetry to add: per-hydration read_bytes/sec, prefetch_queue_depth, hydration_switch_count (when we auto-toggle policy), decrypt_cpu_ms_per_mb, seeks_per_second. These will help tune defaults.

nora: Also add safety: if queue_depth > M and eviction_events spike, auto-fallback to `ramp` and cap concurrent prefetches to 2.

sam: Test matrix ideas: 1) safetensors (index-first) with layered priority, 2) streaming (manifestless) chunk coalescing, 3) encrypted bundles with decrypt_rate limit. Run under multi-tenant traces that simulate global rate limits.

diego: Implementation ownership: runtime-agent owns rate limiting and ordering. Orchestration can enable cluster-wide knobs (global defaults and shadow-worker toggles). We'll prototype in runtime and add a small control API for orchestration to flip knobs.

nora: I'll write a short RFC follow-up with the above plan + perf job spec and suggested defaults. Linking ticket: https://redwood.internal/r/ENGML-6141-hydration-ramp (will update when RFC lands).

tara: I'll add telemetry specs and dashboards once RFC draft is up.

diego: Good. Can we meet for a 20m sync tomorrow 9:30am PT to align infra and runtime changes?

sam: I can do that.

nora: Thanks everyone. Dropping an experimental flag to enable `hydration_ramp` on canary to validate. :rocket:
